title: Azimuthal offsets in spiral arms of nearby galaxies
question: Quantify azimuthal offsets between molecular gas (CO), star formation (Halpha), and stellar mass peaks in spiral arms of nearby galaxies to test and differentiate between spiral arm formation theories.

recipe.goal: Construct spiral arm mask for M51 and adopt PHANGS environmental masks
recipe.method: Identify bright 3.6 um emission along each spiral arm with an unsharp-mask approach, fit an analytic log-spiral function in the galaxy plane, dilate to an empirical width (~1-2 kpc) based on CO emission, and visually extend segments to enforce continuity.

recipe.goal: Measure azimuthal offsets between CO, Halpha, and NIR peaks in radial bins
recipe.method: Divide each galaxy into elliptical annuli of fixed galactocentric radial width matching the coarsest map resolution (~1'' or ~100 pc), subdivide each annulus into azimuthal boxes of matching physical size (~100 pc x 100 pc), compute mean intensity of CO, Halpha, and NIR in each box within each spiral arm mask, find the azimuth of maximum mean intensity for each tracer, and compute the rotation-corrected difference.
key_parameters: radial bin width = max(CO resolution, Halpha resolution), typically ~1'' (~100 pc)
azimuthal box size ~100 pc x 100 pc
assumptions: alpha_CO, R_21 line ratio, and stellar mass-to-light ratio variations at fixed radius within the spiral region are negligible
circular trajectories for gas and stars in the disc plane defined by inclination and position angle

recipe.goal: Classify galaxies by statistical significance of mean offsets and radial trends
recipe.method: Compute mean and standard deviation of offsets across all radii, inner half, and outer half; perform a Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test over 10,000 Monte Carlo runs against a normal distribution centred at zero with the same standard deviation; compute Spearman rank correlation coefficient rho with radius (or angular speed) and running means.
key_parameters: KS test p-value threshold = 0.05 over 10,000 runs
rank correlation coefficient threshold rho < -0.2 with radius

recipe.goal: Fit spiral pattern speeds and star formation timescales for Class A galaxies
recipe.method: Fit a linear relation to the azimuthal offset theta as a function of disc angular frequency Omega = v_rot / R (accounting for error bars) following Egusa et al. (2009) to simultaneously determine the pattern speed Omega_P and Halpha star formation timescale t_Halpha.
assumptions: constant pattern speed Omega_P and constant star formation timescale t_SF across the spiral arm

score_reason: High-level 2D image products (PHANGS-ALMA v4.0 moment-0 maps, S4G ICA maps, PHANGS environmental masks, PAWS maps) are publicly available and the geometric binning algorithm is clearly described, with complete per-galaxy numeric tables provided for verification. However, no analysis code is released, the Halpha dataset is cited as in prep., the new M51 mask is not provided, and exact binning/fitting error bar details are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA data are public 2D moment-0 maps (PHANGS-ALMA DR4), the geometric algorithm for measuring azimuthal offsets in elliptical annuli is straightforward to implement from the text, and comprehensive per-galaxy numerical benchmarks (mean offsets, standard deviations, correlation coefficients, pattern speeds, and star formation timescales) are tabulated.
